main_text.l: igitur infinita animi seruitute nata, educata, in-
stituta natio Hispanica, per se feruens, & chole-
rica, qui potest non fieri sua in religione feruen-
tissima, vel si mauis, sanctissima? imo qui non i-
pse diabolus si Hispanicae inquisitionis esset
capax, semper se in angelum lucis transfigura-
re, aliquemque acquirere Romanae sanctitatis
habitum cogeretur? Hoc ex fonte profluxit
Ignatius de Loyola, qui miles Gallorum virtute in
arce Pompeiopolitana victus: ipse vero super-
stitione omnes vincens, factus est pater Iesuita-
rum, quibus vicissim Gallos, nec non totum orbem
expugnaret terrarum. In Italis vero fre-
quentes illos religionis externos actus oriri de-
prehendes, ex naturali quadam ad hypocrisin
& superstitionem inclinatione: quippe qui, ut
ex omnibus fere suis ipsorum monimentis con-
stat, semper fuerint sintque ad Deorum mul-
titudinem colendam & ad omnem idololatri-
am propensissimi: facile ut appareat, ex hoc eos
fornicationis poculo permulta in religionem
Christianam transfudisse: eamque fere totam
veneno mortifero infecisse. Quo veneno ad-
huc maxima pars orbis Christiani, suauitate,
dulcedine, antiquitate & pulchritudine ipsius

rum confugit Deorum, nimirum & ad innume-

page.notes: Catchword "ipsa," is printed at the lower right, after the last full line; the main text ends with the hyphenated "rei-". The line-end words "fe"/"fua"/"ipfe" etc. are read as long-s spellings (se, sua, ipse). Paragraph division is uncertain: no indents are visible, so the page is taken as one continuing paragraph. Long-s ligatures (ff, ffi) were read as plain s, e.g. "viciffim" as vicissim. The page number is printed in old-style figures ("I2"), read as 12.
